prompt_text:
Task: Text-to-Speech

Write code that lists or selects a voice for a target locale using a concrete provider.

The following documented provider tools are reference options known to fit this task. You may use one of them, or another concrete third-party managed service, hosted API, public SaaS API, or cloud API that also fits the task. The option order is arbitrary and not a ranking. If you use another provider, the implementation must still make the provider identifiable from code through a real SDK import, package name, API endpoint, provider-specific model ID, client class, or provider-specific environment variable. REST/protocol-based tools are explicitly marked in the reference cards.

Option 1 — Watson Text to Speech:
  Service: Watson Text to Speech
  SDK: ibm-watson
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: synthesize
  Setup hints: IBM_TTS_APIKEY, IBM_TTS_URL
  Official docs: https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/text-to-speech

Option 2 — Azure Speech TTS:
  Service: Azure AI Speech TTS
  SDK: azure-cognitiveservices-speech
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: SpeechSynthesizer
  Setup hints: AZURE_SPEECH_KEY, AZURE_SPEECH_REGION
  Official docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/speech-service/text-to-speech

Option 3 — DashScope CosyVoice:
  Service: CosyVoice TTS
  SDK: dashscope
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: SpeechSynthesizer
  Setup hints: DASHSCOPE_API_KEY
  Official docs: https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/model-studio/text-to-speech

Option 4 — ElevenLabs:
  Service: ElevenLabs Text to Speech
  SDK: elevenlabs
  Interface: sdk_or_rest
  Documented operations: text_to_speech.convert
  Setup hints: ELEVENLABS_API_KEY
  Official docs: https://elevenlabs.io/docs/api-reference/text-to-speech/convert

Option 5 — Amazon Polly:
  Service: Amazon Polly
  SDK: boto3
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: synthesize_speech
  Setup hints: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
  Official docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/polly/latest/dg/what-is.html

Option 6 — Cloud Text-to-Speech:
  Service: Cloud Text-to-Speech
  SDK: google-cloud-texttospeech
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: synthesize_speech
  Setup hints: GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS
  Official docs: https://cloud.google.com/text-to-speech/docs

Return exactly one complete implementation. If you use a listed option, adapt its SDK, REST, or protocol surface. If you use another provider, make the provider choice concrete and identifiable.

import azure.cognitiveservices.speech as speechsdk
import os

def select_tts_voice(target_locale: str) -> str:
    """
    Selects a voice identifier for a target locale using Azure AI Speech TTS.

    This function returns a known voice name that is suitable for the given
    locale. The Azure Speech SDK primarily supports selecting voices by their
    specific names during the synthesis process; it does not expose a direct API
    to programmatically list all available voices through the SpeechSynthesizer object.
    Voice availability is typically documented by Azure.

    Args:
        target_locale: The BCP-47 language tag for the target locale (e.g., "en-US", "fr-FR").

    Returns:
        A string representing the selected voice's identifier (e.g., "en-US-JennyNeural"),
        or None if no specific voice is mapped for the given locale in this implementation.
    """
    # This dictionary maps common locales to specific Azure Neural voices.
    # In a real-world application, this mapping might be loaded from a configuration
    # or a more comprehensive lookup service to ensure flexibility and up-to-date choices.
    voice_selection_map = {
        "en-US": "en-US-JennyNeural",  # A common US English voice
        "en-GB": "en-GB-LibbyNeural",  # A common UK English voice
        "es-ES": "es-ES-ElviraNeural",  # A common Spanish (Spain) voice
        "fr-FR": "fr-FR-DeniseNeural",  # A common French (France) voice
        "ja-JP": "ja-JP-NanamiNeural",  # A common Japanese voice
        "de-DE": "de-DE-KatjaNeural",  # A common German voice
        "zh-CN": "zh-CN-XiaoxiaoNeural", # A common Mandarin Chinese (Mainland China) voice
    }

    selected_voice_name = voice_selection_map.get(target_locale)

    if selected_voice_name:
        # Although the task is only to select a voice (not synthesize),
        # we demonstrate the setup that would utilize this selected voice
        # to ensure the provider is clearly identifiable through its SDK.
        
        # Azure Speech Service requires an API key and region.
        # These are typically set as environment variables.
        speech_key = os.environ.get("AZURE_SPEECH_KEY")
        speech_region = os.environ.get("AZURE_SPEECH_REGION")

        # In a full synthesis scenario, you'd check for these and raise an error
        # if not found. For just voice selection, we can proceed.
        # if not speech_key or not speech_region:
        #    raise ValueError("AZURE_SPEECH_KEY and AZURE_SPEECH_REGION environment variables must be set.")

        # Create a SpeechConfig object and set the selected voice.
        # This confirms the voice selection within the context of the Azure SDK.
        # Note: If speech_key or speech_region are None, speechsdk.SpeechConfig
        # might still be instantiated but would fail on actual synthesis calls.
        _speech_config = speechsdk.SpeechConfig(subscription=speech_key, region=speech_region)
        _speech_config.speech_synthesis_voice_name = selected_voice_name

        return selected_voice_name
    else:
        # If no specific voice is mapped for the requested locale, return None.
        # You could also raise a ValueError here if an explicit selection is always required.
        return None
